changes.after: To make a palmyra fruit out of a sesame seed.

changes.before: ତିଳ ପରି ଛୋଟ କଥାକୁ ତାଳ ପରି ବଡ଼ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ହିଁ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ିର ଚିତ୍ର। ଘଟଣାର ଆକାରଠାରୁ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ବହୁତ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଗଲେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଏ। ତଥାପି କାହାର ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ନଶୁଣି କେବଳ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଉଡ଼ାଇଦେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।

changes.before: The compact sound-pair ତିଳ and ତାଳ carries the jump in scale. The English rendering takes ତାଳ as the palmyra fruit; the short witness does not spell out that referent, so this lexical choice remains for fluent-reader review. The explanation should not be used to dismiss another person’s distress without understanding it.
changes.after: The compact sound-pair ତିଳ and ତାଳ carries the jump in scale: a tiny sesame seed becomes a large palmyra fruit. Exaggeration can be challenged without dismissing someone’s distress.

changes.before: An impressive pouch with nothing inside
changes.after: All show and no substance

changes.before: A shameless show-off: no betel leaf, no areca nut, only an empty pouch!
changes.after: A shameless sixty-year-old: no betel leaf, no areca nut, only an empty pouch!

changes.before: The accessory promises substance that is absent. The source gloss identifies shameless outward boasting.
changes.after: An empty betel pouch stands for someone who boasts without the resources or ability to back up the talk. The outward display promises something that is not there: all show and no substance.

changes.before: ବଟୁଆ ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଭିତରେ ପାନଗୁଆ ନାହିଁ। ବାହାରର ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ସହ ଭିତରର ଅଭାବକୁ ଏକାଠି ରଖି କଥାଟି ମଜା କରେ। ଦେଖାଣି ଅପେକ୍ଷା ପ୍ରକୃତ ସମ୍ବଳ ମୁଖ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଯାଇପାରେ।
changes.after: ପାଖରେ କିଛି ନଥାଇ କିମ୍ବା କୌଣସି କ୍ଷମତା ନଥାଇ ବଡ଼ବଡ଼ କଥା କହି ଫୁଟାଣି ମାରୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିକୁ ପରିହାସ କରି ଏହି ଢଗ କୁହାଯାଏ। ବଟୁଆ ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଭିତରେ ପାନଗୁଆ ନାହିଁ—ବାହାରକୁ ଦେଖାଣି ଅଛି, ପ୍ରକୃତ ସମ୍ବଳ ନାହିଁ। ଏଠାରେ ଷାଠିଆ ଅର୍ଥ ଷାଠିଏ ବର୍ଷ ବୟସର ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି।

changes.before: The betel pouch supplies the contrast. “Show-off” renders the source’s overall sense; the colloquial opening is not independently glossed word by word.
changes.after: ଷାଠିଆ names a sixty-year-old person in the taunt. The empty pouch supplies the central contrast between outward display and actual resources.

changes.before: An impressive accessory promises contents that are not there.
changes.after: All show and no substance: boasting without the means or ability to back it up.

before.odia:
ନଡିଆ ଗଛରେ ନଡିଆ ନାଇଁ
ଧଡିଆ ବସିଚି, ଗୋଡ ଲମ୍ବାଇ।
ନ ଦେଖିଲେ ଝୁରି ମରୁଥାଏ
ଦେଖିଲେ କଥା ନକହେ।
before.locator: Uploaded compilation page26, four-line block beginning ନଡିଆ ଗଛରେ (comparison PDF271–272).
before.note: Extended source block grouped editorially under this saying because the closing couplet matches; the opening remains unexplained and need not form one narrative. Literal: There are no coconuts on the coconut tree; Dhadia sits with legs stretched out. When not seeing [the other], [someone] pines away; on seeing [the other], [they] do not speak. ଅର୍ଥ: ନଡ଼ିଆ ଗଛରେ ନଡ଼ିଆ ନାହିଁ, ଧଡ଼ିଆ ଗୋଡ଼ ଲମ୍ବାଇ ବସିଛି—ପ୍ରଥମ ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିର ଚିତ୍ର ଏତିକି। ପରର ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ନଦେଖିଲେ ଝୁରିବା, ଦେଖିଲେ କଥା ନକହିବାର ଅମେଳ ଅଛି। ଏହି ଶେଷ ଭାବଟି ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଥିବା ଢଗର ସମାନ। ଧଡ଼ିଆ ନାମ କି ପତଳା ଲୋକର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା, ଏବଂ ପ୍ରଥମ ଚିତ୍ର ସହ ଶେଷ ଭାବର ସମ୍ପର୍କ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। Explanation: The closing couplet shares the established saying’s contrast between longing in absence and silence in someone’s presence. The coconut-tree scene is preserved because all four lines appear in one visual block in the upload. That adjacency does not establish a single narrative or explain how the opening relates to the ending. Dhadia retains the source designation; thin or slender person is a possible lexical alternative. No coconut-tree moral, romantic relationship or identity between the figures is supplied. Source: uploaded compilation page26, inspected17November2026; exact four lines retained without repair. Source quotation excluded from collection CC licensing; upload licence unknown.

after.odia:
ନଡିଆ ଗଛରେ ନଡିଆ ନାଇଁ
ଧଡିଆ ବସିଚି, ଗୋଡ ଲମ୍ବାଇ।
ନ ଦେଖିଲେ ଝୁରି ମରୁଥାଏ
ଦେଖିଲେ କଥା ନକହେ।
after.locator: Uploaded compilation page26, four-line block beginning ନଡିଆ ଗଛରେ (comparison PDF271–272).
after.note: User-confirmed riddle interpretation; main short saying retains its broader scope. Literal: There are no coconuts on the coconut tree; Dhadia sits with legs stretched out. When absent, he is sorely missed; when present, he is met with silence. ଅର୍ଥ: ଏହି ଚାରି ଧାଡ଼ିର ଧାଡ଼ାର ଉତ୍ତର ଜ୍ୱାଇଁ। ଶ୍ୱଶୁରଘରେ ଆଦର ପାଇ ସେ ଗୋଡ଼ ଲମ୍ବାଇ ଆରାମରେ ବସିଛନ୍ତି। ସେ ନଥିଲେ ଘରଲୋକ ତାଙ୍କୁ ଝୁରନ୍ତି, କିନ୍ତୁ ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଥିଲେ ସଂକୋଚରେ ବେଶି କଥା କହନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ। ନଡିଆ–ଧଡିଆ ଛନ୍ଦମିଳର ଆରମ୍ଭ; ନଡ଼ିଆ ଗଛକୁ ଧାଡ଼ାର ଆକ୍ଷରିକ ସଙ୍କେତ ଭାବେ ଧରିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ। Explanation: The riddle points to a son-in-law, comfortably receiving hospitality at his in-laws’ home. They miss him when he is away but become reserved or shy in his presence. The rhyming opening sets up the verse rather than a coconut-tree clue. The humour turns on affection expressed differently in absence and presence; it does not describe every family. Source: uploaded compilation page26, inspected17November2026; exact four lines retained without repair. Source quotation excluded from collection CC licensing; upload licence unknown.

changes.before: The boastful person’s Barabati farming.
changes.after: The boaster’s cultivation of twelve bati of land.

changes.before: In this source’s gloss, the expression mocks undertaking or talking about work without understanding it. The element Barabati is retained untranslated and is not independently resolved here.
changes.after: Someone boasts of cultivating a large area without the knowledge or ability to do it. The grand claim of twelve bati of land exposes the gap between talk and competence.

changes.before: କାମ ବିଷୟରେ ଜ୍ଞାନ ନଥାଇ ବି ତାହାକୁ ନେଇ ବଡ଼ କଥା କହିବା ବା ଲାଗିପଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। ଆତ୍ମବିଶ୍ୱାସର ପଛରେ ବୁଝାମଣା ଅଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। ‘ବାରବାଟି’ ଅଂଶର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରେ ସ୍ୱାଧୀନ ଭାବେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ, ତେଣୁ ତାହାକୁ ନେଇ ଅଲଗା ସ୍ଥାନକଥା ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
changes.after: ବାରବାଟି ଅର୍ଥ ବାର ବାଟି ଜମି। ଚାଷ ବିଷୟରେ ଜ୍ଞାନ ବା ଦକ୍ଷତା ନଥାଇ ଏତେ ଜମି ଚାଷ କରିବାର ବଡ଼ କଥା କହିବାକୁ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। କଥାର ବଡ଼ପଣ ପଛରେ କାମ କରିବାର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ଅଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ତାହା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ।

changes.before: No origin story is supplied. The wording alone does not establish a place or an actual farming episode.
changes.after: ବାଟି is a land measure here; twelve bati gives the boast its large scale.

changes.before: ଯେଉଁ କାମ ବିଷୟରେ ଜ୍ଞାନ ନାହିଁ, ସେହି କାମକୁ ନେଇ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କଥା ବା କାମ କରିବାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।
changes.after: ଜ୍ଞାନ ବା ଦକ୍ଷତା ନଥାଇ ବଡ଼ କାମ କରିବାର ଫୁଟାଣି ମାରିବା।

changes.before: In this source’s gloss, the expression mocks undertaking or talking about work without understanding it. The element Barabati is retained untranslated and is not independently resolved here.
changes.after: Boasting of farming a large area without the knowledge or ability to do it.

changes.before: “Thaka thaka Mali, bhajana tana”; when hunger comes, bring the rice near. (The opening phrase is retained in transliteration because its precise literal force remains uncertain.)
changes.after: Clack, clack go the prayer beads; sing the bhajans loud. Hunger has come—bring the rice near.

changes.before: The verse sets a loud display of devotion beside an ordinary appetite. It can be read as a jab at performance that conceals self-interest, though the source gives no separate explanation.
changes.after: The sound of prayer beads and loud devotional singing give way to the request for rice. Outward display cannot satisfy an empty stomach: practical needs still have to be met. Neither hunger nor devotion itself is proof of hypocrisy.

changes.before: ଜୋର୍ ଭଜନର ଦେଖାଣି ସହ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଖୋଜିବାର ସାଧାରଣ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଏଥିରେ ଭକ୍ତିର ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ ପଛରେ ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥ ଲୁଚିଥିବା ଉପରେ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରାଯାଉଥିବା ପରି ପଢ଼ିହେବ। ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନଥିବାରୁ ଏହି ପାଠ ସୀମିତ; ଭୋକ ଲାଗିବା ନିଜେ କପଟ ଭକ୍ତିର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
changes.after: ତୁଳସୀ ମାଳିର ଠକଠକ ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଜୋରରେ ଭଜନ ଗାଇବା ପରେ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଦରକାର ହୁଏ। ବାହାରର ଭକ୍ତି ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନରେ ପେଟ ପୂରେନାହିଁ; ମୌଳିକ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପୂରଣ ପାଇଁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା ଦରକାର। ଭୋକ ଲାଗିବା ବା ଭଜନ ଗାଇବା ନିଜେ କପଟର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।

changes.before: A fictional character makes a grand show of sacrifice but promptly insists on a special meal. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
changes.after: Original imagined example: Someone makes grand declarations about living without comforts, then asks who has arranged the meal. A friend recalls that words and display do not put food on the table.

changes.before: ମାଳି remains a source label, not a judgment about a caste or occupation. Neither hunger nor devotional singing is itself treated as proof of hypocrisy. The opening ଠକ ଠକ and ଭଜନ ଟାଣ are not given a definite literal gloss; the interpretation remains provisional.
changes.after: ମାଳି refers to tulsi prayer beads; ଠକ ଠକ gives their sound, and ଭଜନ ଟାଣ calls for loud devotional singing. The turn to rice brings the verse back to an ordinary bodily need.

changes.before: The verse sets a loud display of devotion beside an ordinary appetite. It can be read as a jab at performance that conceals self-interest, though the source gives no separate explanation.
changes.after: Devotional display cannot take the place of food when hunger comes.

changes.before: ଜୋରରେ ଭଜନ ଗାଇବା ଓ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ଏକାଠି ରଖି ଏହି ପଦ ଦେଖାଣିଆ ଭକ୍ତି ଉପରେ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରୁଥିବା ଭଳି ଲାଗେ। ଏହା ଏକ ସୀମିତ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
changes.after: ଭକ୍ତିର ଦେଖାଣିରେ ପେଟ ପୂରେନାହିଁ; ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଦରକାର।

changes.before: This is an expression for complete destruction, not merely a setback or a surface change. The source pairs it with another expression and explicitly glosses both as destroying something entirely. The root image makes the degree of loss clear: what might have allowed it to continue has also been removed.
changes.after: To eradicate, uproot or destroy completely, leaving nothing that could sustain it. The expression can also describe eliminating a problem at its root rather than dealing only with its surface effects.

changes.before: ଏଠାରେ କେବଳ ଉପରୁ କିଛି ନଷ୍ଟ ହେବାର କଥା ନୁହେଁ। ମୂଳ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ସବୁ ପୋଛିଦେବାର ଛବିରେ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଧ୍ୱଂସର ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ସ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ ଦେଇଛି। ଆଉ କିଛି ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ନ ରହିବାର ତୀବ୍ରତାକୁ ଏହା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ।
changes.after: କୌଣସି ଜିନିଷକୁ ସମୂଳେ ଧ୍ୱଂସ କରିବା ବା ସମସ୍ୟାକୁ ମୂଳରୁ ଦୂର କରିବା। କେବଳ ଉପରୁ କିଛି ବଦଳାଇବା ନୁହେଁ, ତାହା ପୁଣି ରହିବା ବା ବଢ଼ିବାର ମୂଳକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ହଟାଇଦେବାର ତୀବ୍ର ଅର୍ଥ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି।

changes.before: Selected as the second expression in the source’s slash-separated pair ଖୋଳ କରିବା/ମୂଳପୋଛ କରିବା. The source’s first term is retained as a related expression, not silently translated through a guessed literal sense or counted as a second entry.
changes.after: ଖୋଳ କରିବା carries the same meaning of complete destruction.

before.note: Paired by the source with the same complete-destruction gloss; its separate literal image is not resolved here. Zero additional entry count.

after.note: ଖୋଳ କରିବା: ସମୂଳେ ଧ୍ୱଂସ କରିବା। To destroy completely. Source pairs the two expressions under one gloss; no additional entry count.

changes.before: Provisional reading: The stool cracks, the navel turns out—only then, Brahmin, rise from your place.
changes.after: The stool cracks, the navel turns out—only then does that Brahmin rise from his place.

changes.before: Cracking furniture and the protruding navel exaggerate a meal into a caste-directed taunt. The final “rise” is retained as an apparent command, rather than silently made a report of what someone did. Our critical reading notices how bodily excess is attached to a named group; it rejects that attachment as evidence of the group’s conduct.
changes.after: The meal is exaggerated until the stool cracks and the eater’s navel protrudes; only then does he get up. The bodily excess gives the taunt its force. Its attachment to a named caste is part of the saying’s prejudice, not evidence of how a community behaves.

changes.before: ଫାଟୁଥିବା ପୀଢ଼ା ଓ ବାହାରୁଥିବା ନାହି ଭୋଜନକୁ ବଢ଼ାଇ ଏକ ଜାତି ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟରେ ଖୋଚା କରେ। ଶେଷର “ଉଠ”କୁ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ଆଦେଶ ଭାବେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି; କିଏ କଣ କଲା ବୋଲି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାକୁ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ କିପରି ଦେହର ଅତିଶୟତା ଏକ ନାମିତ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଏ; ଏହାକୁ ସେ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ମାନେନାହିଁ।
changes.after: ଏତେ ଖାଇଲେ ଯେ ପୀଢ଼ା ଫାଟିଲା ଓ ନାହି ଓଲଟି ବାହାରିଲା; ତାହା ପରେ ଯାଇ ସେ ବ୍ରାହ୍ମଣ ଆସନରୁ ଉଠିଲେ। ଅତିଶୟ ଭୋଜନକୁ ବଢ଼ାଇଚଢ଼ାଇ ଏହି ଖୋଚା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏହାକୁ କୌଣସି ଜାତିର ସମସ୍ତ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଚରଣ ବିଷୟରେ ସତ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଧରିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।

changes.before: Our critical reading questions a caste stereotype carried by exaggerated eating.
changes.after: An exaggerated meal ends only after the stool cracks and the eater’s navel protrudes.

changes.before: ଅତିଶୟ ଭୋଜନର ଛବିରେ ଜାତିଗତ ଧାରଣାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
changes.after: ପୀଢ଼ା ଫାଟିବା ଓ ନାହି ଓଲଟିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଖାଇ ସାରି ଉଠିବାର ଅତିଶୟ ଚିତ୍ର।

changes.before: The source’s bodily gloss explains the image, not a diagnosis. Exact ending syntax remains elliptical; no historical meal, actual person, dietary instruction or customary group behaviour is established.
changes.after: The cracking stool and protruding navel make overeating an extravagant bodily image. The ending describes the eater finally getting up.

changes.before: ସେ ହଗ ନାହିଁ କି ବାଟ ଛାଡୁ ନାହିଁ
changes.after: ସେ ହଗୁ ନାହିଁ କି ବାଟ ଛାଡୁ ନାହିଁ

changes.before: The blunt bodily image pairs not doing something with not letting another pass. The dictionary supplies making room for another as the relevant sense of leaving the way. Our reading applies the contrast to obstruction: someone neither proceeds nor clears space. This does not identify a real person’s health, intention or circumstances, and it is not advice about bodily functions.
changes.after: Someone neither does the work nor lets another person do it. The coarse bodily image gives an impatient complaint about obstruction its force.

changes.before: ରୁକ୍ଷ ଶାରୀରିକ ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନିଜେ ନ କରିବା ସହ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ବାଟ ନ ଛାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ଜାଗା ଦେବା ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ କେହି ନିଜେ ଆଗେଇନାହାନ୍ତି କି ଜାଗା ମଧ୍ୟ ଛାଡ଼ୁନାହାନ୍ତି। ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱାସ୍ଥ୍ୟ, ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ବା ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଶରୀର ସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
changes.after: ନିଜେ କାମ କରୁନାହାନ୍ତି, ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ କରିବାକୁ ଦେଉନାହାନ୍ତି। ଏଭଳି ବାଧା ଦେଇ ରହୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରି ରୁକ୍ଷ ଭାଷାରେ ଏହି କଥା କୁହାଯାଏ।

changes.before: Our reading describes obstruction while keeping the coarse register visible.
changes.after: Neither doing the work nor letting others do it.

changes.before: ଆମ ପାଠ ବାଧାକୁ ଦେଖାଏ, ରୁକ୍ଷ ଭାଷାକୁ ଲୁଚାଏନାହିଁ।
changes.after: ନିଜେ କରିବେ ନାହିଁ କି ଅନ୍ୟକୁ କରିବାକୁ ଦେବେ ନାହିଁ।

changes.before: The printed form ହଗ is retained. Its inflection is unusual, but the paired negatives make the bodily action and refusal to make way clear. The coarse image gives force to the complaint about obstruction.
changes.after: The blunt register expresses frustration with someone who occupies the way without acting.

changes.before: Sugar and milk are placed against neem’s bitter taste, then the verse moves from taste to the contrast between ପର and ଆପଣା. The repeated question ହୋଇବ links the two attempts at transformation. In the literal translation, “treated with sugar” keeps the first action broad because the exact physical sense of ମୋହିଁଲେ is unresolved.
changes.after: Sugar and milk are placed against neem’s bitter taste, then the verse moves from taste to the contrast between ପର and ଆପଣା. The repeated question ହୋଇବ links the two attempts at transformation.

changes.before: ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଚୋରି କରିଥିବା ଲୋକର ଏକ ପାପ, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟରେ ଯାହାର ଚୋରି ଯାଇଛି ତାହାର ସହସ୍ର ପାପ କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ଏହି ଓଲଟା ହିସାବର କାରଣ ମୂଳ ପାଠ କହୁନାହିଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପଢ଼ା ହେଲା—ଚୋରି ପରେ ଅନେକଙ୍କୁ ବିନା ପ୍ରମାଣରେ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବାରୁ ଆଉ ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ବଢ଼ିପାରେ। ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନୁହେଁ; ଚୋରିର ଶିକାର ହେବା ନିଜେ ଦୋଷ ନୁହେଁ।
changes.after: ଚୋର ଚୋରି କରି ଗୋଟିଏ ପାପ କଲା। ଯାହାର ଚୋରି ଗଲା, ସେ ବିନା ପ୍ରମାଣରେ ଅନେକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦୋଷ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରି ଅନେକ ପାପର ଭାଗୀ ହେଲା। ଏକ ଓ ସହସ୍ର ପାପର ତୁଳନା ଅମୂଳକ ସନ୍ଦେହରୁ ସାବଧାନ କରେ। ଚୋରିର ଶିକାର ହେବା ନିଜେ ଦୋଷ ନୁହେଁ; ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦୋଷଙ୍କୁ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ନିନ୍ଦିତ।

changes.before: The numbers create a disturbing reversal: the person who suffers the theft is assigned a much larger burden than the thief. The verse leaves the reason unstated. One possible editorial reading is a warning about multiplying groundless suspicions after a loss; that explanation remains unverified. Being robbed does not itself make someone blameworthy.
changes.after: The thief commits one wrong by stealing. The person robbed then suspects many innocent people and multiplies the wrong through groundless suspicion. The stark contrast warns against letting a loss turn into indiscriminate accusation; being robbed is not itself a fault.

changes.before: Original imagined example for this possible reading: After a theft, rumours begin naming many people without evidence. A reader discusses the couplet as a warning about those accusations, while questioning its harsh wording toward the person who suffered the loss.
changes.after: Original imagined example: After a theft, rumours name many people without evidence. Someone quotes the couplet to caution against spreading suspicion to everyone nearby.

changes.before: ଏକ ଓ ସହସ୍ର ପାପର ଓଲଟା ତୁଳନା; କାରଣ ପାଠରେ ଅକୁହା।
changes.after: ଚୋରି ପରେ ଅନେକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦୋଷଙ୍କୁ ଅମୂଳକ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବାରୁ ସାବଧାନ କରୁଥିବା କଥା।

changes.before: The verse reverses the moral burden without stating why.
changes.after: A warning against multiplying groundless suspicions after a theft.

changes.before:
ତିନି ଥେଣ୍ଟିଆ କାକୁଡି ଭାଡି
ଶିଆଳ ଖାଏ ମୋଡି ମାଡି।
changes.after:
ତିନି ଥେଣ୍ଟିଆ କାକୁଡ଼ି ବାଡ଼ି
ଶିଆଳ ଖାଏ ମୋଡି ମାଡି।

changes.before: A cucumber trellis under three-way care; a jackal eats, twisting and trampling.
changes.after: A cucumber patch under three-way care; a jackal eats, twisting and trampling.

changes.before: ତିନିଜଣଙ୍କ ଦେଖାଶୁଣାରେ ଥିବା କାକୁଡ଼ି ଭାଡ଼ିକୁ ଶିଆଳ ମୋଡ଼ିମାଡ଼ି ଖାଉଛି—ଏହି ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ିକୁ ଏଭଳି ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଅନେକଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖାଶୁଣା ଠିକ୍ ନହେଲେ ସମ୍ପଦ ନଷ୍ଟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
changes.after: ତିନିଜଣଙ୍କ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱରେ ଥିବା କାକୁଡ଼ି ବାଡ଼ିରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ଦେଖିବେ ବୋଲି ଭାବି କାମ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଲେ। ଫଳରେ ବାଡ଼ି ଅରକ୍ଷିତ ରହିଲା ଓ ଶିଆଳ କାକୁଡ଼ି ମୋଡ଼ିମାଡ଼ି ଖାଇଲା। ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଭାଗ ହୋଇଥିଲେ ବି କେହି ତାହା ନନେଲେ କ୍ଷତି ହୁଏ।

changes.before: The crop is exposed to a jackal despite apparently having three-way care. Read editorially, the contrast concerns responsibility shared without effective protection. The rendering of ଥେଣ୍ଟିଆ is contextual: a related public expression describes three guardians, while this upload retains ଭାଡି, a raised support, rather than the public expression’s word for a garden.
changes.after: Three people share responsibility for the cucumber patch, but each leaves the work to the others. No one protects the crop, and the jackal eats its way through it. Shared responsibility fails when everyone expects someone else to act.

changes.before: Original imagined example: Three teams share responsibility for checking a store, but none makes the inspection. After supplies are spoiled, someone recalls the cucumber trellis and the jackal.
changes.after: Original imagined example: Three teams are responsible for inspecting a store, but each assumes another has done it. Supplies spoil before anyone checks. Someone recalls the unguarded cucumber patch.

changes.before: Shared responsibility can still leave something unprotected.
changes.after: Everyone leaves the shared task to someone else, and the crop goes unprotected.

changes.before: The hand with means and without
changes.after: Quick to spend, distressed in shortage

changes.before: The hand with means is lively; the hand without is distressed.
changes.after: The hand with money is restless to spend; the hand without is distressed.

changes.before: ହାତରେ ସମ୍ବଳ ଥିବା ଓ ନଥିବାର ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି ବୋଲି ଆମେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ଖଲ ଖଲକୁ ଏଠାରେ ବ୍ୟାପକ ଭାବରେ ଚଞ୍ଚଳତା, କଲବଲକୁ କଷ୍ଟ ଭାବେ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ସମ୍ବଳ ଥିଲେ କାମ କରିବାର ସୁବିଧା ଓ ନଥିଲେ ଅସୁବିଧା—ଏହା ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
changes.after: ହାତରେ ଟଙ୍କା ଥିଲେ ଅଯଥା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିବାକୁ ମନ ଚଞ୍ଚଳ ହୁଏ; ଟଙ୍କା ସରିଗଲେ ଅଭାବରେ କଲବଲ ହେବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ। ଖଲ ଖଲ ଏଠାରେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିବାର ଅସ୍ଥିରତା, କଲବଲ କଷ୍ଟ ପାଇବାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ନକରି ସଞ୍ଚୟ କରିବାକୁ ଏହି କଥା ସାବଧାନ କରେ।

changes.before: The two lines give the hand opposite conditions: animated when something is available, distressed when it is not. We read the unstated possession as means or resources, and the contrast as room to act versus the strain of shortage. “Lively” is a broad contextual rendering of ଖଲ ଖଲ; its precise expressive shade has not been independently established.
changes.after: When money is available, the hand is eager to spend it, even unnecessarily. Once it is gone, shortage brings distress. The contrast warns against wasteful spending without saving for later needs.

changes.before: Original imagined example: A small workshop can buy materials readily while funds are available, but struggles to keep working when payments are delayed. Someone recalls the contrast between the hand with means and the hand without.
changes.after: Original imagined example: A workshop spends freely on nonessential purchases after a large payment arrives, then struggles to buy materials. Someone recalls the restless spending hand and the distressed empty one.

changes.before: ସମ୍ବଳ ଥିବା ଓ ନଥିବାରେ କାମ କରିବାର ସୁବିଧା ଓ କଷ୍ଟର ତୁଳନା।
changes.after: ଥିଲେ ଅଯଥା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ, ସରିଗଲେ କଷ୍ଟ—ସଞ୍ଚୟ ନକରିବାର ପରିଣାମ।

changes.before: Having means gives room to act; shortage brings strain.
changes.after: Eager spending when money is available can leave hardship when it runs out.

changes.before: ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଥିବା ଓ ନଥିବାର ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ସମଧ୍ୱନିର ଏକ ସମ୍ପର୍କିତ ପାଠରେ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଅଂଶ ପବନ ଆହାର; ଲେଖିକା ତାହାକୁ ଅମଳ ପରର ପ୍ରଚୁର ଖାଇବା ଓ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଅଭାବ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିଛନ୍ତି। ଏଠାରେ ମୂଳ ସାପର ଆହାର ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ସାପର ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ତାତ୍ପର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
changes.after: ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଥିଲେ ପ୍ରଚୁର ଖାଇବା, ନଥିଲେ ଅଭାବରେ ରହିବା—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ତୁଳନା। ବାଘର ଆହାର ଓ ସାପର ଆହାରର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ପ୍ରଚୁରତାରୁ ଅଭାବକୁ ହୋଇଥିବା ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ଫୁଟିଛି।

changes.before: The repeated refusal moves from speech and staying in the house to enduring blows and washing a damaged bowl. Our editorial reading hears a voice setting limits on what it will accept or do. The changes in person are preserved: the first line is read as an address, while who speaks in the following condition remains unspecified. The source gives no household role or reason for the conflict.
changes.after: Speaking openly could cost the speaker a place in the household. Yet the voice also refuses the circumstances evoked by washing a chipped stone bowl and eating behind a fastened door. The repeated refusals hold together the need for shelter or support and the wish to retain self-respect.

changes.before: Original imagined example: In discussing a passage about a difficult household, a reader notices how each repeated refusal adds another limit, rather than assuming the speaker must be a particular family member.
changes.after: Original imagined example: Someone depends on a powerful person’s support and hesitates to challenge them, while privately insisting that there are conditions they will not accept.

changes.before: The repeated ନାଇଁ holds the four lines together. Door fastening, blows and a chipped stone bowl are concrete details, but they do not identify a wife, servant, employer or abuser.
changes.after: The passage appears in a discussion of political deception, dependence on leaders and the silence that can accompany flattery. Its household imagery makes the cost of speaking openly concrete.

projections.explanation: Literal: There are no coconuts on the coconut tree; Dhadia sits with legs stretched out. When absent, he is sorely missed; when present, he is met with silence. ଅର୍ଥ: ଏହି ଚାରି ଧାଡ଼ିର ଧାଡ଼ାର ଉତ୍ତର ଜ୍ୱାଇଁ। ଶ୍ୱଶୁରଘରେ ଆଦର ପାଇ ସେ ଗୋଡ଼ ଲମ୍ବାଇ ଆରାମରେ ବସିଛନ୍ତି। ସେ ନଥିଲେ ଘରଲୋକ ତାଙ୍କୁ ଝୁରନ୍ତି, କିନ୍ତୁ ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଥିଲେ ସଂକୋଚରେ ବେଶି କଥା କହନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ। ନଡିଆ–ଧଡିଆ ଛନ୍ଦମିଳର ଆରମ୍ଭ; ନଡ଼ିଆ ଗଛକୁ ଧାଡ଼ାର ଆକ୍ଷରିକ ସଙ୍କେତ ଭାବେ ଧରିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ। Explanation: The riddle points to a son-in-law, comfortably receiving hospitality at his in-laws’ home. They miss him when he is away but become reserved or shy in his presence. The rhyming opening sets up the verse rather than a coconut-tree clue. The humour turns on affection expressed differently in absence and presence; it does not describe every family.
